findings.title: Retry cleanup is not restricted to SMS reminders
findings.body: The new `OR` branch deletes every `WorkflowReminder` with `retryCount > 1`, regardless of its method, scheduled state, or scheduled date. This cron is specifically the SMS scheduler and the previous cleanup was scoped to `method: SMS`; as written, any email/WhatsApp reminder (or another producer using this field later) with a retry count above one will be silently deleted by the SMS cron. Restrict the retry-count branch to unscheduled SMS reminders so this job cannot remove unrelated workflow work.

findings.title: Retry count updates can be lost when cron executions overlap
findings.body: The handler reads `retryCount` in `findMany` and later writes `reminder.retryCount + 1`. Concurrent or overlapping cron requests can select the same reminder with count 0, both fail scheduling, and both write 1. The reminder has then failed twice but is treated as having failed once and continues being retried; concurrent executions can also repeatedly attempt the same SMS. Use an atomic database increment (and ideally atomically claim/transition an unscheduled reminder) rather than a stale read-modify-write value.

findings.title: Exception-path retry update has the same lost-update race
findings.body: The catch path also persists a value calculated from the count captured before scheduling. Two overlapping failing invocations overwrite each other with the same value, so exceptions do not reliably advance the retry limit either. This path should use the same atomic increment/claim mechanism as the non-throwing failed-response path.
